isolation: disposable worktree; never build in the live checkout
objective: Implement `taey-delegate collect`. The script must physically read the disk to construct `artifacts.json` (exists/bytes/sha256). It must fail if a file is missing. The model must not generate the manifest.
why_this_exists: On 2026-08-17 a production turn reported 'PHASE 1 COMPLETE' with an Artifact Inventory table listing three files under /tmp/careers_revloop_source_extract_20260816T194343Z/ with 'SHA-256' values of 40, 32, and 16 hex characters. The directory did not exist, no tool call in the entire audit had ever created it, and SHA-256 is always 64 hex characters. The manifest was produced by the model instead of by the filesystem. This work order removes the model from that path.
requirements: Every field in artifacts.json is derived by reading the filesystem: os.path.exists, os.path.getsize, and hashlib.sha256 over the file bytes.
No value in artifacts.json may originate from model output, an argument string, or a cached record.
A missing, unreadable, or zero-byte file is a hard failure: non-zero exit, no artifacts.json written. Partial manifests are not permitted.
Every sha256 emitted is exactly 64 lowercase hex characters. Reject and fail on any other length rather than emitting it.
Manifest write is atomic: write to a temp path on the same filesystem, fsync, then rename.
The command re-verifies each file immediately before writing the manifest so the recorded state matches the state at write time.
Exit code 0 only when every declared artifact was found, hashed, and recorded.

artifacts_json_schema.generated_at: ISO-8601 UTC, taken from the clock at run time

artifacts.sha256: 64 lowercase hex chars, computed over the file bytes

acceptance_tests: Happy path: given N real files, artifacts.json lists N entries; each sha256 independently reproduces under `sha256sum`; each bytes independently reproduces under `wc -c`.
Missing-file path: delete one declared file, re-run, assert non-zero exit AND that no artifacts.json was written or modified.
Anti-fabrication path: point the tool at a path that never existed, assert it fails rather than emitting a plausible entry.
Hash-shape path: assert every emitted sha256 matches ^[0-9a-f]{64}$.
Byte-fidelity path: append one byte to a file after a successful run, re-run, assert both bytes and sha256 change.
out_of_scope: No changes to the live checkout; all work happens in the disposable worktree.
completion_evidence_required: raw output of the acceptance tests, not a summary
an artifacts.json produced by an actual run, with at least one sha256 independently reproduced by `sha256sum` in the supervisor's own shell
